uncited: Slice Plane Ordering is a rendering rule that dictates the draw order of transparent volume slices to ensure correct alpha blending and occlusion.
It solves the problem of transparent objects appearing blended in front of obscured objects when rendered in arbitrary order.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Plane Composing Algorithms](2154-plane-composing-algorithms.md) by focusing strictly on the temporal draw sequence relative to the camera, rather than the geometric assembly of the slices themselves.
- Slice spacing is uniform, defined by the grid structure from [Plane Slicing](845-plane-slicing.md).
The logic ensures that slices are processed in an order that respects the back-to-front requirement for alpha blending, handling the camera crossing the volume bounds.*
- If depth testing is disabled, the depth of the slices does not occlude one another.
